transcript: Place a handful of raw rice inside a glass and leave it behind your bedroom door for seven days. What happens to those grains will show you something invisible about the place where you sleep. Rice is one of the most sacred foods in ancestral traditions. It represents abundance, protection, and balance. But what most people do not know is that raw rice works as a natural energy sensor. It absorbs what is in the environment and shows it through its appearance. Do this, take a clear glass, and fill it halfway with white raw rice. Not cooked, not washed, just as it comes from the package. Hold the glass with both hands and say in silence, show me what I cannot see. Absorb what is heavy in this place. Place the glass behind your bedroom door where nobody will touch it. Leave it there for seven days without moving it. After seven days, look at it carefully. If the grains are yellowish, dark, or have spots that were not there before, your room was heavy. The energy was dense and the rice pulled it toward itself. If it has a strange smell or moisture, even though it never touched water, the weight was even greater. Accumulated tension badly slept nights that left a mark on the space. If the rice is still clean, dry, and white as when you placed it, your room is balanced. Do not cook that rice. Wrap it in paper and throw it away outside the house. Wash the glass with salt and water. If it darken, repeat for another week, and compare. Many people notice that in the second week, the rice wakes up clearer. A sign that the space is gradually being cleaned. Write in the comments, I will place the rice today if you are going to do this, and come back in seven days to tell me what you found. And if you feel that it is not just your room that is heavy, but you on the inside, the rice shows you what is outside. But what is inside only gets clean when you learn to release what you have been carrying. I spent over 20 years learning in silence how to do exactly that, and everything I know is inside the way back to stillness. The link is in my profile.
